items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S9039

SPONSOR: BIAGGI
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the civil rights law, in relation to establishing a
cause of action for unlawful interference with protected rights

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

To protect the rights of individuals seeking abortion care or gender
affirming care in New York State.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Names this bill as the "freedom from interference with repro-
ductive and endocrine health advocacy and travel exercise act", or the
"FIRE HATE act".

Section 2. Describes the harm that can be imposed upon people exercising
their right to travel to NYS for the purposes of reproductive services
and abortion healthcare.

Section 3. Amends the Civil Rights law by adding section 70-b.

Section 4. Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The legislature finds that the rights of the residents of the State of
New York are imperiled by actions which would attempt to or purport to
prevent or limit travel to New York for the exercise of rights protected
by the New York State Constitution and the laws of the State of New
York, or which would put those who travel to New York at risk of civil
actions and criminal actions brought in Courts outside the State of New
York seeking to punish or impose civil liability on individuals for
traveling to New York to exercise individual and human rights protected
within the State of New York.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 6 Chapter 218
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 9039-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the civil rights law, in relation to establishing a
        cause of action for unlawful interference with protected rights"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill is aimed at providing critical protections for residents of
the State of New York as well as those who may travel  to  New  York  to
exercise  rights protected by the state constitution and state laws. The
legislation creates a cause of action for the unlawful interference with
protected rights by permitting persons who have exercised or facilitated
the exercise of rights protected in New  York,  such  as  the  right  to
obtain  reproductive or endocrine health care, and have nonetheless been
subjected to civil or criminal suits under the  laws  of  another  state
limiting such conduct, to bring a lawsuit in New York for damages.
 
  I  strongly support the goals of this legislation. Other states in the
nation seek not only to prohibit reproductive freedoms within their  own
borders,  but  also  to  punish those who may travel to New York to seek
reproductive and endocrine health care here. I am committed to  ensuring
that  New York remains a safe haven for those individuals as well as the
New Yorkers who facilitate such care. While Roe v. Wade may be poised to
fall and other states in  the  nation  enforce  overreaching  laws  that
attempt  to  undermine  the  rights and values we cherish, it is crucial
that we provide a legal remedy to recover damages in such instances.
 
  However, as written, the  bill  did  not  provide  sufficient  clarity
regarding  the  damages  available  when  suits  filed under the laws of
another state were done so with malicious intent or  intent  to  harass,
intimidate  or  punish  the  exercise of rights protected under New York
law.  I have secured an agreement with the Legislature to make technical
changes clarifying the additional damages that may be recovered in  such
instances.
 
  On the basis of this agreement, I am proud to sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
